_README: Published numbers for learned/RL compression methods (MEM1, BACM-RL/FoldAct,
PEEK, ...), overlaid next to our heuristic-ladder rows at aggregation time.
These methods are NOT rungs (see the top-level README): they never decomposed
timing vs. selection, so where they land relative to H3/Oracle is the finding.
1. Every entry MUST carry full provenance (paper, arxiv, table). An entry
whose 'score' is null is treated as UNVERIFIED and is printed as a TODO,
never as a number. Nothing here may be typed from memory -- transcribe it
from the exact cited table so it is auditable.
2. 'metric' names the EXACT one of our own result keys the number is
comparable to. MEM1's eval.py sums per-objective F1 across objectives and
means over examples => that is our 'mem1_table_summed_f1', NOT *_mean_f1.
3. Every overlaid number is caveated automatically with 'caveats' below,
because these baselines used a different (full-corpus) retrieval setup
and, for some, a different backbone than our fixed Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.
A raw win/loss vs. these numbers is NOT evidence about compression-policy
quality until the confounds below are controlled (see README no-caveat tier).

caveats.retrieval_scope: Published baselines retrieved over a FULL corpus (e.g. the whole Wikipedia dump via a dense E5/FAISS index for MEM1 & Search-R1). Our harness retrieves over each example's small bundled gold+distractor pool (~10-32 paragraphs) so the Oracle is constructible. Their search task is strictly harder; our absolute scores are therefore NOT directly comparable. This confound cancels only when the learned baseline is re-run inside our harness against our retriever.
caveats.backbone: Numbers are reported for the method's own backbone (often an RL-trained Qwen2.5-7B, or a larger instruct model used as a baseline). Our ladder is a frozen Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. A backbone mismatch alone can move F1 by more than any policy effect we measure.
caveats.task_composition: MEM1's multi-objective tasks compose NQ + HotpotQA (and others) into an N-objective sequence; a single dataset label here ('hotpotqa') is an approximate, not exact, match to that composed distribution.
caveats.eval_protocol: Only compare against a baseline number using the metric key named in its 'metric' field. Never place a standard_qa_* number next to these; they are SQuAD-style diagnostics, not the MEM1 protocol.
